notes.note: Discard warns, then discards; never blocked. When later hunks in the plan list the hunk in needs, the host sends their numbers with the confirm request and the webview's confirmation names them ('Hunks 4 and 6 need this hunk'). With no dependents, a plain confirmation. The contract's host<->webview messages carry the dependent hunk numbers.

Working tree drift (edge case, keep it minimal): before every stage/unstage/discard the host runs git apply --check for that hunk. On failure the action is refused and the host sends a 'stale' state; the webview shows a 'Files changed since this plan was made' banner with a Rerun review button (recollect hunks + replan) and disables actions until the rerun completes. No file watcher, no plan merging. The contract's messages include the stale state and the rerun request.

Contract schemas are shape-only. The plan layer owns every content rule, in plan.md's order. A stage count outside 1..12 is reported as '✗ stages: <n> stages, use 1 to 12 …' (plan.md has no message for it, so this is the chosen wording). Stage has no breaking field; plans never carry '!'.
ScratchIndex.apply returns one result per hunk in order and keeps trying later hunks after a failure; the plan layer reports a ✗ order line for each failed hunk.

Skill is { body, references }: body = SKILL.md text, references = map of file name (PLAN.md, STAGES.md, WRITING.md) to text. The provider layer loads skill/ into this shape and does not change the contract.

Webview actions reference hunks by id; the host resolves file and first line for Open file. ReviewState.currentStage and ReviewStage.commitMessage/committed drive Skip, Commit and the pre-filled message.
